name: Shalmaneser
overview: Shalmaneser was a male king of Assyria, as recorded in 2 Kings 17:3. Beyond his royal status, Scripture does not provide additional tribal or personal details about him. His role as king places him within the historical context of Assyrian dominance during the period described in the Old Testament.
namesAndTitles: The name Shalmaneser means 'Shulman is chief' or 'Sulmanu is leader,' reflecting a designation of authority and leadership. His title, King of Assyria, straightforwardly identifies his political and military role as the ruler of the Assyrian empire, as noted in 2 Kings 17:3.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Shalmaneser beyond his identification as King of Assyria. There are no listed relatives or tribal affiliations associated with him in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Shalmaneser is significant in the biblical narrative primarily as the Assyrian monarch who played a key role in the unfolding history of Israel and Judah. His reign marks a period of Assyrian expansion and influence, which had direct consequences for the Israelite kingdoms. His mention in 2 Kings 17:3 situates him within God's sovereign plan, demonstrating how earthly rulers are instruments in the divine orchestration of history.
